children: Thailand's inflation accelerated in August as energy prices rose.

The consumer-price index increased 2.53% from a year earlier, government data showed Monday. That was up from a 1.95% rise in July and above the 2.31% gain forecast by economists polled by The Wall Street Journal.
Core inflation, which excludes volatile fresh-food and energy prices, accelerated to 1.44% in August, up from 1.34% in July.
Headline inflation reached a more than three-year-high in April but subsequently eased, remaining within the Bank of Thailand's 1%-3% target range.

Global oil prices edged higher in August amid renewed fighting in the Middle East and concerns about potential supply disruptions. Thailand is particularly exposed to fluctuations in global energy prices crisis because it relies heavily on imported oil.

The BOT's monetary-policy committee voted unanimously in August to keep its policy rate at 1.00%, balancing a temporary, supply-driven pickup in inflation against subdued domestic demand and low and uneven economic growth.
The central bank said it would continue monitoring developments in the Middle East, the extent to which businesses pass higher costs on to consumers and medium-term inflation expectations.

With inflation remaining within the BOT's target range and the recent increase in prices largely reflecting temporary supply-side pressures, the central bank is likely to look through the effects, DBS economists said in a recent report.
They expect the BOT to maintain its accommodative monetary-policy stance for the rest of the year to support the country's uneven economic recovery.
